title: Bumble and Glint's Canyon Adventure
markdown:
The sun burst through Bumble’s window and painted his bedroom gold.

“Wahoo,” Bumble boomed, bouncing out of bed with a thump. Today felt different. It was the perfect day for an adventure. He shoved open the barn door. Birds trilled. The air smelled fresh. Dewdrops sparkled. Dandelions puffed out their sunny scent.

Then he saw it, way up high, on a skinny dusty ledge in Whispering Canyon: his dad’s old brown leather map case. It must have fallen on their last trek through the prickly plains. The canyon was deep. The ledges looked about as wide as a blade of grass. Bumble gulped. He was not the best hopper. His hooves wobbled when things got tricky. A shiver of nerves tickled his spine.

A flash of emerald zipped past his snout.

“Bumble. What’s buzzing?” Glint the gecko, tiny feet a blur, scales like a thousand little emeralds. He always looked ready.

“Glint. My map case. Stuck way up there.” Bumble pointed a hoof at dizzying heights. The canyon walls looked like grumpy giant faces. A low rumble echoed from the bottom.

Glint’s curious eyes blinked. “Whoa. That’s a big hop for any bison.”

“I know.” Bumble’s shoulders slumped. “My hooves get all wobbly on skinny places. I might tip over.” He pictured a comical tumble, down, down, down.

Glint grinned and scurried up Bumble’s leg as if it were a friendly tree. “But you’re strong. And I’m really good at gripping.” He wiggled sticky toes. “Let’s do it together.”

Bumble’s heart did a happy flip-flop. Together sounded much better.

They trotted bravely to the canyon’s edge. The ground dropped away below. The wind whistled and whooshed. It played a swirling tune through the rocks. Bumble looked at the first ledge. It was just a sliver. So small. He took a deep steadying breath and puffed out his chest.

“Okay, Glint. On the count of three.”

“One,” Glint chirped, tiny body tensed for action.

“Two.” Bumble braced himself. He dug his hooves into the dirt.

“Three.” They sprang. Bumble landed with a bit of a wobble. His knees buckled slightly. But Glint clung tight to his back, like a super-sticky backpack. They had not toppled.

They hopped again. And then again. Each ledge was trickier and skinnier than the last. Bumble’s knees felt like wobbly jelly. His breath came in short panting bursts.

“I don’t think I can make it to the next one,” he panted. His voice trembled just a little.

“Yes you can,” Glint squeaked, full of pep. “Look. Just one more big jump. You’re almost there.”

Bumble looked up. He saw it. The map case. So close he could almost touch it. But the gap between them and the ledge was wider. A bit of a scary gap for a wobbly hopper like him. A tingle crept up his neck. What if he missed?

“I’ll go.” Glint zipped off Bumble’s back, a tiny green arrow across the gap. He landed perfectly. Sticky toes held. He nudged the map case with his nose.

A huge gust puffed through the canyon. Whoosh. The map case wobbled wildly, ready to plunge.

“Glint,” Bumble yelled, voice echoing.

With a mighty shove, Glint tipped the case. It tumbled toward Bumble. Wobbly knees protested. He stretched a hoof as far as it would go. Thump. He caught it. The precious map case was safe.

“We did it,” Glint cheered, doing a tiny jig on the ledge. “You caught it.”

Bumble grinned, clutching the heavy case. He had hopped the tricky ledges. He had not tipped. Bubbly bravery filled him from hooves to horns.

“That was amazing, Glint.”

“No. You were amazing.” Glint scampered back down Bumble’s leg. “You were brave even when your hooves felt wobbly.”

They trotted out of Whispering Canyon. Sun warmed their backs. The map case sat secure under Bumble’s hoof. Hearts still thumping.

“Today,” Bumble declared, lifting the case, “is going to be spectacular.”
